item.title: Toji: Kyoto's Tallest Pagoda and Great Flea Market — Guide
item.description: Toji, ‘the East Temple’, was founded in 796 when Kyoto became the capital and given to the great monk Kukai, who made it a centre of esoteric Shingon Buddhism. Its five-story pagoda, rebuilt in 1644, rises 55 metres and is the tallest wooden tower in Japan, a landmark visible from the shinkansen and an emblem of the city. Inside its Lecture Hall stands a three-dimensional mandala of twenty-one carved deities arranged by Kukai himself.

item.title: Kofukuji: The Five-Story Pagoda of Nara — Guide
item.description: Kofukuji, founded by the Fujiwara clan and moved to Nara in 710, was once among the most powerful temples in Japan, and its five-story pagoda — at 50 metres the second-tallest wooden pagoda in the country — is an icon of the city, rising beside Sarusawa Pond at the very entrance to Nara Park. Beyond the pagoda and the rebuilt Central Golden Hall, the temple’s greatest treasure is its National Treasure Museum, home to a celebrated collection of ancient Buddhist sculpture including the beloved three-faced, six-armed Ashura statue, one of Japan’s most admired religious artworks.

item.title: Saishoin Five-Story Pagoda: Hirosaki's Elegant Landmark — Guide
item.description: The five-story pagoda of Saishoin temple in Hirosaki is an Important Cultural Property and one of the most beautiful in northern Japan. Built in the 17th century, its slender vermilion tiers are especially lovely framed by spring cherry blossoms. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hirosaki, Aomori Hours Grounds daytime; ~9:00–16:30 Admission Free (grounds) Time needed 30–45 minutes Best time Spring (cherry blossoms) What to See The elegant 17th-century five-story pagoda, an Important Cultural Property.
